title: ‘Jurassic Park': Using AI, scientists try reviving extinct Wolves, Woolly mammoths
content: Colossal Biosciences is pioneering efforts to resurrect extinct species through cutting-edge technologies like CRISPR. Their recent success in recreating dire wolf embryos by utilizing DNA from ancient fossils combined with gray wolf cells showcases their innovative approach. With plans to birth woolly mammoths within the next decade, the company aims for ecological benefits, including the preservation of Arctic permafrost, promising exciting advancements in the field of extinct species reproduction.

title: Chethan Kumar in Parallax: Why countries sometimes need to reinvent the wheel
content: With countries increasingly depending on technology imports, worries over control and access to essential systems intensify. This dependence on external vendors can expose nations to risks during times of geopolitical instability or supply chain hiccups. Creating local alternatives may not always be cost-effective, yet it aids in establishing self-reliance. The case of India's UPI underscores the critical need for developing solid financial tech infrastructures.

title: Nevada man turned roadside junk into desert home now visited as free attraction
content: Thunder Mountain Monument in Nevada features sculptures created from discarded materials by Frank Van Zant. This unique roadside attraction developed from his personal vision to honor Native American history. After a fire in 1983, the site faced preservation challenges until it was recognized as a historic site in 1992. The monument is maintained today with visitor donations and a caretaker's assistance.

title: Florida oyster reef bounces back: 0 to 244 oysters/m² in 5 years
content: Florida’s Lone Cabbage Reef, once a vibrant oyster habitat, faced severe decline before restoration efforts. Researchers rebuilt the reef in 2018 using dolomite limestone to create suitable surfaces for oyster larvae. Subsequent studies documented significant increases in oyster populations over five years, reaching densities of 244 oysters per square metre. The restoration benefited local fisheries, generating substantial economic impact and employment opportunities.

title: Salesforce CEO renames company’s biggest product after US govt's 'enemy post'

The order requires all federal agencies to adopt this new terminology in their documents and public discourse.

title: Beyond Jaisalmer: 6 Rajasthan winter gems to plan now

From thrilling tiger safaris at Ranthambore National Park to the breathtaking sights from a hot-air balloon, the state is brimming with activities. Mount Abu’s pleasant climate serves as a perfect getaway, while Jodhpur's heritage walks and wildlife encounters in Jawai enhance the experience. The vistas from Sajjangarh Palace are simply the cherry on top.

title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee released late night after being detained in Gurgaon

title: California flying saucer house built in 1969 lists for nearly $1.5 million
content: Nestled in California's stunning landscape, the Donaldson Futuro is a captivating flying saucer-shaped home now listed for $1.495 million. Constructed in 1969, this architectural marvel exemplifies space-age design and carries historical weight. After languishing in neglect, it was expertly restored by Milford Wayne Donaldson, preserving its mid-century essence while integrating modern comforts. This is a unique opportunity to embrace a landmark of architectural history.

title: Lake Tahoe ranch once listed for $188m now prepares separate $43m mansion sale

The property was initially priced at $188 million but has seen a price reduction to $125 million. Potential buyers are now interested in purchasing parts of the estate instead of the entire property. The government aims to reduce the steel industry's carbon-emission intensity by nearly 39 percent by 2047. To achieve this goal, India will secure raw materials through overseas investments and joint ventures. The draft policy includes measures for diversifying sourcing to mitigate supply risks.

title: How Peter Pan has funded a children's hospital for 97 years
content: In 1929, J. M. Barrie selflessly granted the rights to Peter Pan, establishing a perpetual source of funding for Great Ormond Street Hospital. The hospital benefits from the story's performances, facilitating care for critically ill children. A unique UK law safeguards this donation, ensuring royalties persist beyond copyright expiry. Barrie's ties to the hospital remain influential, demonstrating the power of literature in sustaining charitable endeavors.

title: US hospital worker paid $15.99 for Goodwill painting; later valued up to $80,000

title: 165-million-year-old fossil reveals mammal ancestor with modern feeding traits

Named Megacauda sungei, the Jurassic-era animal could chew and swallow food using specialised structures. Published in Nature, the findings offer new insights into how early mammals developed different feeding abilities.

Current missile defense systems face significant challenges when intercepting hypersonic missiles, which can change trajectories mid-flight. title: Trump throws another tantrum about not getting Nobel, declares war on Norway
content: the u.s. president denounced Oslo for an "indelible stain" on its reputation . he also dismissed this year's winner, Navi Pillay, as a woman . the move was aimed at ending the threat the "rogue court" posed to U.S. sovereignty .

title: ‘Blatant attack': Press bodies condemn detention of journalists at Delhi protest
content: four journalists’ organisations expressed concern over the detention of journalists covering protests in Delhi demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation . journalists were targeted while documenting the police action . they alleged reporters carrying valid press identity cards were taken away and some had their phones and reporting equipment confiscated .

title: SIR stir: 'Kashmir model' in Delhi, situation akin to Emergency, says opposition
content: CM Omar Abdullah says the "Kashmir model" has reached the capital . former CM mehbooba mufti calls the crackdown a reminder of Kashmir's 2019 lockdown . he calls the conditions "akin to the emergency"

title: 'Interference in internal affairs': India rebukes UN body over Delhi crackdown
content: india rejects the UN human rights body's concerns over the security crackdown ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's proposed protest in Delhi . the ministry of external affairs calls them "unwarranted" and an "unacceptable interference" in the country's internal affairs .

title: 'No breach of peace for one year': Delhi court's condition for release of Team CJP
content: the leaders are set to hold a press conference at 2pm on Sunday . a bail bond of Rs 50,000 was filled for "maintaining peace and good behaviour" the leaders were detained from their flight shortly after they landed in the national capital .

title: Turkey bans social media for under-15s
content: the decision was published in the official state journal on saturday, October 10, following the passage of a law by parliament in April . under the legislation, social media providers must introduce safeguards to protect young users . the law requires platforms to “take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement” protections .

title: Restrained, detained, contained: Clampdown foils stir, thousands confined to home
content: phalanxes of 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel and a virtual choke on metro services and trains foiled the march to Jantar Mantar . young protesters detained on their way to the protest site and bundled into buses and vans, kicking and screaming, through the day .

title: CJP announces protests across country, starting with Mumbai's Shivaji Park today
content: ajinkya Shinde announced a protest in Mumbai against the detention of leaders and protesters across Delhi and other parts of the country . in a post on X, he said protesters would assemble at T Junction in Shivaji Park on Sunday .

title: 'Sikh sentiments hurt': Gurdwara body questions protesters for intrusion into premises
content: the dSGMC chief slams protesters and police over the incident . he alleged some protesters entered the premises with placards and raised slogans . the incident "hurt Sikh sentiments," he said .
